claim:
Let \(1<p<\infty\), and let \(X_p=(\mathbb R^2,N_p)\) be the real Day--James plane
\[
N_p(u,v)=
\begin{cases}
\bigl(|u|^p+|v|^p\bigr)^{1/p},&uv\ge0,\\
|u|+|v|,&uv\le0.
\end{cases}
\]
For the Baronti--Casini--Papini constant
\[
A_2(X_p)=\sup_{x,y\in S_{X_p}}\frac{N_p(x+y)+N_p(x-y)}2,
\]
the known value is
\[
A_2(X_p)=1+2^{1/p-1}.
\]
Moreover, the complete equality set is rigid:
\[
\frac{N_p(x+y)+N_p(x-y)}2=1+2^{1/p-1}
\]
holds if and only if
\[
\{x,y\}=\{\varepsilon e_1,\delta e_2\}
\qquad
\text{for some }\varepsilon,\delta\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
Thus, for every \(1<p<\infty\), the only \(A_2\)-maximizing pairs are the two coordinate-axis unit vectors, up to order and independent sign changes of the two vectors.
integrity: The proof independently tracks equality through the exact upper-bound argument, then excludes nonextreme boundary points by convexity. Numerical sampling was used only as a stress test and is not part of the proof.
scientific_limitations: The equality classification is for the real Day--James family with 1<p<infinity and the Baronti--Casini--Papini constant A_2 only. The p=1 endpoint and the general James-type parameters are not classified.
title: Rigidity of \(A_2\)-extremizers in the Day--James \(\ell_p-\ell_1\) planes
